title: from research paper to the big screen
summary: ramayana brings visual dubbing to a global cinema audience. explore the epic’s rollout and the research journey from Wav2Lip to sync. labs.
body_markdown:
Some stories have been crossing borders for centuries. Ramayana is one of them.


The ancient Sanskrit epic, traditionally attributed to Valmiki, has travelled through languages, performance traditions and generations of retellings across India and Southeast Asia. Its story of Rama, Sita and Ravana is part of a living cultural inheritance. Every new telling finds another way to bring audiences into that world.[\[1\]](https://www.larousse.fr/encyclopedie/oeuvre/Ramayana/140258)


Now, a new theatrical adaptation is taking that journey onto screens around the world. Alongside its scale, cast and visual effects, Ramayana is putting another part of filmmaking in the spotlight: visual dubbing.


## an epic built for a global audience


Directed by Nitesh Tiwari and produced by Namit Malhotra, Ramayana stars Ranbir Kapoor as Rama, Sai Pallavi as Sita and Yash as Ravana. Prime Focus Studios announced the first film’s worldwide theatrical arrival on November 5, 2026. Hans Zimmer and A.R. Rahman composed the score, with DNEG leading the visual effects.[\[2\]](https://www.primefocusstudios.com/news/the-journey-begins-ramayana-part-one-arrives-worldwide)[\[3\]](https://ramayanariseofalegend.com/home/)


The investment reflects that ambition. CNN reported an estimated $500 million budget across the two-film adaptation. That figure covers both parts, rather than the first release alone.[\[4\]](https://kesq.com/entertainment/cnn-style/2026/11/08/the-500-million-gamble-to-make-indias-ramayana-a-global-phenomenon/)


Audiences are already showing up. As checked on November 10, the numbers listed approximately $72.7 million in worldwide box office, including $13.85 million in the North American market. These are early reported theatrical grosses, which will continue to change as the release unfolds. Ticket sales are also shared with exhibitors and distributors, so they do not equal money returned to the producer.[\[5\]](https://www.the-numbers.com/movie/Ramayana-Part-1-(2026-India))


Sony Pictures is handling the international release. Listings include North America, Australia, New Zealand, Germany and the Netherlands, with a Hindi and English release also announced for the UK. Prime Focus’s launch announcement confirms six release languages: Hindi, Tamil, Telugu, Kannada, Malayalam and English.[\[5\]](https://www.the-numbers.com/movie/Ramayana-Part-1-(2026-India))[\[6\]](https://www.mediahouseglobal.com/news/ramayana-rise-of-a-legend-arrives-in-uk-cinemas-this-november)[\[2\]](https://www.primefocusstudios.com/news/the-journey-begins-ramayana-part-one-arrives-worldwide)


## when the image speaks another language


Traditional dubbing records dialogue in a new language. Visual dubbing takes the process into the picture, adapting a performer’s visible mouth movements to the new spoken words.


For Ramayana’s English version, Malhotra told CNN that the actors recorded their own English dialogue. Motion capture and AI were then used to align mouth and facial movements with the speech, in a process overseen by Brahma AI. The voices, he said, were performed by the actors rather than generated by AI.[\[4\]](https://kesq.com/entertainment/cnn-style/2026/11/08/the-500-million-gamble-to-make-indias-ramayana-a-global-phenomenon/)


That makes this release a significant moment for the medium. Visual dubbing is becoming part of how filmmakers plan an international theatrical experience, alongside translation, voice performance and distribution.


## from a research paper to the big screen


Long before visual dubbing became part of a global film rollout, researchers were working on a deceptively difficult problem: making a face in an existing video match a different audio track, even when the system had never seen that person before.


In 2020, K R Prajwal, Rudrabha Mukhopadhyay, Vinay P. Namboodiri and C V Jawahar published the research behind Wav2Lip. The model used a trained lip-sync expert to guide the generation of mouth movements, and the paper introduced benchmarks for evaluating whether audio and picture actually matched.[\[7\]](https://arxiv.org/abs/2008.10010)


Prajwal and Rudrabha later co-founded sync. labs with Prady Modukuru and Pavan Reddy. The company, founded in 2023, carried that research background into tools for editing speech and lip movements in video.[\[8\]](https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/sync-2)[\[9\]](https://f.inc/portfolio/sync-labs/)


The path from research to cinema has involved many teams and approaches. By 2025, visually dubbed features such as Watch the Skies were reaching US theaters. Ramayana now brings the medium into the conversation around a major international epic.[\[10\]](https://newsroom.notified.com/gul-pr/posts/pressreleases/svensk-langfilm-forst-i-varlden-med-visuell-a)


For filmmakers, that progress opens a creative possibility: preparing dialogue for a new audience with greater freedom over the words, while keeping the visual performance connected to what they hear.


The original Wav2Lip paper, 2020. K R Prajwal, Rudrabha Mukhopadhyay, Vinay P. Namboodiri and C V Jawahar. Source: arxiv.org/abs/2008.10010.


## the next chapter is international


Ramayana has always travelled through retelling. This release adds another chapter: audiences in different countries encountering the same characters through words performed in their own language, with the image adapted to meet them there.


Visual dubbing gives filmmakers another way to invite people into a story. Translators shape its meaning. Actors give the dialogue emotion. Artists bring sound and picture together. The technology creates new room for that collaboration.


As the medium develops, its most exciting possibility is a wider audience for stories rooted in a particular place, culture and imagination.
